methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having completed an IPO on the Tokyo exchange. The comparable universe for this company is limited. While the Drones & Autonomous sector contains five peers total, the comp set is dominated by private companies—specifically Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—with zero public peers identified. No public tickers exist for direct comparison.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable to Terra Drone. Despite identifying five same-sector competitors, none met the screening thresholds required for robust triangulation: zero companies matched same-stage criteria, zero matched adjacent-stage criteria, and zero fell within similar valuation tiers. Peer-median analysis requires a minimum of three datapoints within narrow filters to avoid false precision; this threshold was not met. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the heterogeneity of business models, scale, and development stage within drones and autonomous systems.

The absence of both public comparables and a sufficiently tight private peer set materially constrains valuation inference for Terra Drone. Additional methods—such as precedent transactions among the five identified peers, discounted cash flow analysis using company-specific assumptions, or transaction multiples from the venture funding rounds of Zipline, Joby, Nuro, Archer, and Elroy Air—would be required to establish a defensible valuation range. The Tokyo IPO context and founder Toru Tokushige's operational profile would also inform appropriate discount or premium adjustments, but cannot substitute for underlying financial or comparable data.
